help.title: Help
help.basicsBody:
Encrypt: Switch to the Encrypt tab, select the files or folders to encrypt (multiple items may be selected at once), enter a password, and click Encrypt.

Decrypt: Two methods are available — double-click the .locked marker file left at the original location, or locate the item in the Encrypted Items tab and use its unlock button.

Encrypted Items: View all currently encrypted items, decrypt them individually, permanently delete them, and review the complete activity history.
help.howItWorksBody:
Once encrypted, content is relocated to a centrally managed storage area (the Vault). Only a marker file named .locked remains at the original location; it contains no original content and merely indicates that an item was previously stored there. When encrypting a folder that already contains .locked marker files, the existing locked items are preserved individually and can be found and unlocked separately from the Encrypted Items list.

Three independent unlock methods are available and may be enabled simultaneously: password (required; the remaining two are optional), Passkey (rapid unlock via this device's Windows Hello), and recovery key (a one-time backup code for emergency use).

The Vault location may be changed in Settings to a cloud-synced folder (for example, OneDrive), allowing multiple devices to share encrypted content through your sync client for cross-device backup. The password itself is never synchronized and must be remembered independently.
help.precautionsBody:
A forgotten password results in permanent data loss. This is an intentional design choice — no backdoor exists, and no party, including the developer, is able to assist with recovery.

A Passkey is bound to the device on which it was created and cannot be used on another device; the password or recovery key must be used instead.

The recovery key is displayed only once. Once the screen is closed, it cannot be retrieved again — copy, save, or record it immediately.

"Permanently Delete" in the Encrypted Items list irreversibly destroys the encrypted content rather than merely removing it from the list. Deletion requires password confirmation before it proceeds, and this action cannot be undone.
help.criticalActionBody: Critical Action Verification can be enabled in Settings. Once enabled, destructive operations such as clearing activity history require Windows Hello verification before they can proceed; if also enabled, moving the Vault location is gated behind the same verification. Disabling this feature likewise requires passing Windows Hello verification first, preventing anyone who already has access to the device from simply turning off this protection.
help.folderGuardBody: Folder Guard is a separate feature from encryption — it restricts a folder purely through Windows access permissions, without encrypting its contents. It only stops casual browsing, not a determined attacker bypassing permissions; use Encrypt for anything sensitive. The first time you use it, set a shared password on the Folder Guard tab, and optionally enable Passkey for quick unlocking afterward. Locked folders can be unlocked one at a time or all at once from the same tab; unlocked entries can be opened directly in Explorer via "Open Folder", or locked again with "Lock Again". If you forget the password and Passkey isn't available either, you can still manually reclaim access via Explorer's Properties → Security → Advanced — this isn't encryption, so there's no unrecoverable risk. The settings page also has an advanced toggle, "Open locked folders with a .lockfolder file": when enabled, locking a folder creates a companion ".lockfolder" marker file next to it — double-clicking that file pops up the unlock prompt directly and opens the folder automatically on success, without switching back to FileLocker first or hitting an "Access Denied" error. The folder's own access restriction is unaffected by this toggle.
